q: The quantity that determines how cold or hot an object is is _____.
e: The quantity that determines how cold or hot an object is is temperature. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Heat: energy that flows because of a temperature difference.

q: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called _____.
e: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called thermometers. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred involving instruments.

q: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as _____.
e: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as heat. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Internal energy: the capacity to do work.
Heat is the energy in transit. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the _____ to the second body.
e: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the first body to the second body. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the _____ of that matter.
e: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the internal energy of that matter. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work. Thermal energy: the capacity to do work.

q: Temperature is a measure of the _____ energy of molecules.
e: Temperature is a measure of the internal energy of molecules. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred. Kinetic: energy a body has because it is moving.
